title: Two ants side by side, with what differs at the top
question: Is this the comparison you'd want? The dimmed block underneath is everything the two have in common -- would you rather it were not there at all, or is it worth having to see what did NOT vary?
context_md:
HOLD on one row, pin another, press VS.

**Read the bright block at the top and you have the answer in about four seconds**: ant 37 ranged 124 cells against 89, dug 17 against 2, and delivered *nothing* while ant 27 delivered 7. One is wandering and digging, the other is actually bringing food home.

That ordering is the whole page and I got it wrong first time. Kept in the natural order, the two ants put **fourteen identical plain-speech lines above the nine rows that differed** -- so a page you open to ask 'why is this one doing better' answered below the fold. Differences first, matches dimmed underneath.

I also suppress the usual cell page while this is open. It is the only page that gets that treatment: its own left-hand column *is* the pinned ant's cell page, so leaving both up drew the same numbers twice and ate the width that makes the comparison readable.

One wart worth knowing about: rows whose label carries a frame number (F630 FIRST FED) can never pair up, so each ant contributes its own row with -- opposite. It reads correctly and it does inflate the difference count by one per event.

items.label: COMPARE
items.caption: Ant 37 held, ant 27 pinned. Bright rows differ, dim rows match.
